newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's SFC says surveillance of market adequate.
newsitem.headline: HK's SFC says surveillance of market adequate.

text.p: Legislators told Hong Kong's securities watchdog to be more strict in dealing with stock market manipulation, but a Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) official said on Monday that the move was unnecessary.
"I think the surveillance of suspected market manipulation and investigation of it is quite adequate at the moment," SFC executive director Gerard McMahon told government radio.
Legislators met McMahon in a financial panel discussion on Monday, the radio said.
The call for more strictness followed an enquiry begun last week by the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong over unusual trading activity at the open of last Thursday's session.
The Hang Seng Index surged 213 points to 13,744.30 in the first 15 minutes of trade but ended the day 31.57 points down at 13,499.38.
"We survey the market virtually minute by minute," McMahon told the radio.
Paul Phenix, executive director of the exchange's compliance division, said an enquiry was made in response to some unusual price orders put in on Thursday. He declined to comment further.
Phenix told Reuters last week that the exchange was examining the opening transactions of a number of stocks and asking the brokers involved to explain what took place.
Local newspapers said six houses were being queried.
An SFC spokesman said there was concern about the developments but declined to say whether any investigation would be launched.
"After the exchange's enquiry, if it finds suspicion of any irregularities, the case will be passed to the SFC to follow up," an SFC source said.
